learningObjective: Understand what `torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic` does and how it interacts with recompilation.

canonicalClaims.claim: `torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(t, dim)` tells Dynamo to treat that dim as symbolic during tracing (using a SymInt), producing a compiled graph parameterized in that dim and installing a symbolic-shape guard so multiple sizes share the same graph.
conditions: The traced computation is compatible with symbolic-shape codegen (no path forces specialization).
nonImplications: Does not imply guarantees of one-compile-fits-all; other dims can still specialize.
Does not imply the symbolic-shape kernel is as fast as a size-specialized one.

misconceptions.claim: mark_dynamic disables all guards on the tensor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only the marked dim becomes symbolic; other guards remain.
Rank is unchanged; only the dim's compile-time treatment is adjusted.
It remains an active API in current releases.

misconceptions.claim: mark_dynamic and `dynamic=True` do exactly the same thing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: `dynamic=True` is a compile-time setting; mark_dynamic marks a specific tensor's specific dim.

implementationFacts: `torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(tensor, dim, min=None, max=None)` can also carry bounds
Automatic-dynamic promotion after N recompiles is a related mechanism
SymInt values propagate through the traced graph and reach Inductor codegen
performanceScenarios: Marking known-varying dims dynamic avoids recompile storms in production; overusing it may miss size-specific optimizations.
